content.value_statement: Complex implementation plans can lose quality when tasks move forward without review. This skill coordinates subagent execution with spec and code quality checks.
actual_capabilities: Defines when to use subagent execution for independent implementation tasks.
Outlines a repeatable loop for dispatching implementer subagents.
Requires questions to be resolved before implementation begins.
Adds spec compliance and code quality reviews before task completion.
Provides task dispatch and review templates for consistent handoffs.
limitations: Requires a completed implementation plan before use.
Works best when tasks are mostly independent.
Does not replace project-specific architecture decisions.
Does not provide automated testing or review tooling by itself.

use_cases.title: Run a planned feature build
use_cases.description: Split independent tasks across subagents while keeping review gates in the same session.

use_cases.title: Enforce implementation review order
use_cases.description: Require spec compliance review before code quality review for each completed task.

use_cases.title: Manage multi-file cleanup work
use_cases.description: Assign isolated refactors and verify changes before moving to the next item.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple subagent task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-driven-development for this completed plan. Dispatch one implementer for the first independent task, then run spec and quality reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate independent tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-driven-development with this task list. Identify independent tasks, dispatch implementers one at a time, and stop when a review fails.

prompt_templates.title: Run review-gated implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-driven-development for this plan. For each task, include context, acceptance criteria, test needs, spec review, and quality review.

prompt_templates.title: Recover from review failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-driven-development after a failed review. Send the issues back to the same implementer, request fixes, and repeat both reviews.

output_examples.input: Completed plan for three independent interface tasks.
output: The first task is dispatched with context and acceptance criteria.
The implementer answers questions before editing starts.
Spec and quality reviews decide whether the task can complete.

output_examples.input: Task passes implementation but fails spec review.
output_examples.output: The same implementer receives the issues, fixes them, and repeats both reviews before progress continues.
The final review checks overall changes, integration tests, documentation, and merge readiness.

best_practices: Prepare acceptance criteria before dispatching any implementer.
Answer subagent clarification questions before edits begin.
Complete spec review before code quality review.
anti_patterns: Skipping review steps when the implementation appears complete.
Starting code quality review before checking requirements.
Continuing to the next task with unresolved review issues.

faq.question: Does this skill write code itself?
faq.answer: No. It defines an orchestration workflow for assigning implementation tasks to subagents.

faq.question: Should I use it without a plan?
faq.answer: No. The skill expects a completed implementation plan with clear tasks.

faq.question: Can tasks run in parallel?
faq.answer: The skill is designed for current-session orchestration and sequential review gates.

faq.question: Which reviews are required?
faq.answer: It requires spec compliance review and code quality review for each task.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It asks the implementer to include testing, but project commands must come from the user or repository.

faq.question: Is it suitable for urgent fixes?
faq.answer: It can help when the fix has clear acceptance criteria. Very small changes may be faster with direct implementation.
